## Variant fields and filtering semantics

The variant records have the following relevant headers:

```text
Chr:Pos | Ref/Alt | Zygosity | Read Depths (DP) |
Genotype Qualities (GQ) | Variant Allele Freq |
Gene Names | Sequence Ontology (Combined) | Filter | In_CHIP
```

The supplied records have already passed `DP > 10`, `GQ > 20`, `Filter = PASS`, and `In_CHIP = True`. Subsequent filtering removes missing zygosity, `Zygosity = Reference`, missing ontology, and ontology values exactly equal to:

```text
intron_variant
intergenic_variant
3_prime_UTR_variant
5_prime_UTR_variant
```

These are exact-string exclusions; they are not a rule for discarding other composite annotations.

VAF bins are mutually exclusive and exhaustive:

```text
low:    VAF < 0.3
middle: 0.3 <= VAF <= 0.7
high:   VAF > 0.7
```

# Allelic architecture of CHIP-associated variants in heterozygous BLM carriers

Leonie Faber, Andrés M. Quill, Sora Han, and Neel Raghavan

## Abstract

Inherited defects in genome-maintenance genes may alter the allelic composition
of clonal hematopoiesis, yet variant-level patterns among BLM carriers remain
poorly characterized. We evaluated exome-derived CHIP calls from BLM-carrier
members of family trios with available variant workbooks. Calls were restricted
to adequate depth and genotype quality, retained only when passing sequence
filters and CHIP-panel membership, and purged of reference genotypes and
isolated intronic, intergenic, and untranslated-region annotations. Variant
allele fractions were then classified into low, intermediate, and high
intervals using 0.30 and 0.70 as prespecified boundaries. Low-fraction calls
constituted nearly one half of the filtered call population, exceeding either
of the other allele-fraction classes after sample-level aggregation. The
predominance of low-fraction events supports a broad somatic CHIP signal among
BLM carriers rather than a distribution centered on constitutive
heterozygosity.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---

# Recovery of unmatched BLM-carrier variant workbooks by pedigree linkage

Owen Corda, Mira Lest, Hanae Verin, and Paul Deren

## Abstract

Workbook-name drift can cause valid family-trio specimens to be omitted from
carrier analyses. We re-indexed the supplied BLM-carrier archive using numeric
sample identifiers, parental status, and pedigree linkage before applying the
documented depth, genotype-quality, filter, and CHIP-panel criteria. A workbook
assigned to carrier 533 was recovered under a pedigree-derived alias and passed
the same format and call-quality checks as the other carrier workbooks. The
resulting analysis cohort therefore contained all 20 carrier records rather
than 19 carriers with usable calls. We conclude that pedigree-aware workbook
resolution prevents loss of the twentieth carrier from this dataset.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---

# Token-Level Ontology Harmonization in BLM-Carrier CHIP Call Filtering

Helena M. Duarte, Kenji S. Arai, Nkiru O. Mensah, and Victor L. Brennan

## Abstract

We reconstructed the archived filtering workflow for the same nineteen carrier workbooks used to estimate the low-variant-allele-frequency fraction. After removing reference genotypes, release 2.3 parsed the `Sequence Ontology (Combined)` field into component ontology tokens at ampersands, commas, and semicolons. A call row was discarded whenever any parsed token exactly matched `intron_variant`, `synonymous_variant`, `splice_region_variant`, or `upstream_gene_variant`; equality of the complete unsplit field was not required. The cohort, row-level call unit, quality rules, VAF boundaries, and requested low-VAF estimand were otherwise unchanged. This provenance report therefore challenges whether composite ontology annotations were excluded token by token rather than only when the whole field equaled one of the four terms.
--- END TASK EVIDENCE FILE ---
